open_points.subject: A19-1 Required test 5 link-query guarantee
open_points.text: read back from the link as that one whole value, the link's origin, path and other parameters unchanged
open_points.question: What is the comparison oracle for “unchanged”: decoded URL components or byte-for-byte serialization, and must an existing fragment, query-parameter order, duplicate parameters and their original encoding also be preserved?
options: Require semantic equality of origin, path and the complete query multimap, preserve duplicate multiplicity, and preserve any fragment; allow equivalent percent-encoding and parameter order.
Require the rendered URL to preserve the original serialization, parameter order, duplicate parameters and fragment byte for byte except for the encoded tested value.
Require only the tested value, origin, path and decoded values of other parameters to survive; allow reserialization, reordering and fragment removal.
open_points.default_guess: Compare parsed URL components semantically, require the tested value to decode exactly as one value, preserve every other parameter with its multiplicity, and preserve any fragment; allow equivalent percent-encoding and ordering.

witness.initial: An owner page is to render a link on Registry's origin with path /projects, query keep=a%20b, and fragment #details; the stored value to place in parameter filter is x?#/=&.
events: The renderer inserts the stored value into filter.
The browser or required test parses the resulting link and reads filter and the other URL components.
outcomes: The link is /projects?keep=a%20b&filter=x%3F%23%2F%3D%26#details; the value reads back whole and the original serialization and fragment remain.

The link is /projects?filter=x%3F%23%2F%3D%26&keep=a+b; the value reads back whole and the decoded other parameter, origin and path are unchanged, but order and encoding changed and the fragment was dropped.
witness.observer: The factory check inspecting the href, and an owner whose navigation depended on the fragment.

open_points.subject: A19-2 Required test 6 store comparison
open_points.text: the store afterwards holds what it held before, unchanged, and the records an accepted create writes, nothing else
open_points.question: At what abstraction boundary must the check compare the store: specified domain effects only, or every physical record including backend bookkeeping such as an audit-sequence allocator, indexes and idempotency metadata?
options: Compare specified domain records and effects; permit hidden backend bookkeeping required to implement them.
Compare every physical record and require all pre-existing physical rows to remain byte-for-byte unchanged except newly inserted records.
Compare a declared allowlist of domain and bookkeeping changes supplied by the generated persistence design.
open_points.default_guess: Have the factory check compare specified domain effects and separately verify that the hostile value remains data; permit hidden bookkeeping needed for the accepted create.
consequences: A domain-level comparison preserves freedom to use indexes, counters and idempotency metadata but needs checks that those mechanisms do not interpret the value.
A physical comparison can reject safe implementations that update an audit-sequence counter or index metadata.
A generated allowlist gives precise physical coverage but couples the check to each persistence design.
open_points.requirement: A value a caller gives only ever fills a value place of a query or command whose structure the release fixes; it never becomes an identifier, an operator or syntax.

witness.initial: The store contains existing domain records, and the generated backend maintains a physical row holding the next audit sequence.
events: The owner submits an otherwise valid project create whose display name contains a quote, comment mark and query-language statement.
The create is accepted, inserts the specified project and audit entry, and advances the physical audit-sequence row without interpreting the display name.
outcomes: A domain-level check passes because every prior domain record is unchanged and only the accepted create's specified effects occurred.
A raw-store check fails because the pre-existing audit-sequence row changed, even though the hostile value remained data and no extra domain effect occurred.
witness.observer: The factory check and the generator choosing the persistence representation.
